answer: One concrete mechanism: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because ridge only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, tide is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any glacier approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
